title.value: Social Neuro AI: Social Interaction as the 'Dark Matter' of AI
title.justification: The title clearly reflects the main topic of the paper, which is about the importance of social interactions in the development of AI, akin to 'dark matter' in their complexity and essential nature.
title.quote: Social Neuro AI: Social Interaction as the 'dark matter' of AI

extractions.description: The paper presents a framework for incorporating biological examples of social learning mechanisms into AI, emphasizing that social interactions are largely unexplored but crucial for developing advanced cognitive abilities in AI. The authors propose 'Social NeuroAI' as a field to focus on socially intelligent agents through biological plausibility, temporal dynamics, and social embodiment.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on social interactions and cognitive development within AI, which does not fit into any of the predefined eco-responsible categories focused on climate change and sustainability.
primary_category.quote: However, the field of AI has mostly embraced a solipsistic perspective on intelligence. We thus argue that social interactions not only are largely unexplored in this field but also are an essential element of advanced cognitive ability, and therefore constitute metaphorically the “dark matter” of AI.

primary_sub_category.justification: The primary focus on social learning and interactions in AI development does not match any listed sub-categories related to environmental or sustainable topics.
primary_sub_category.quote: We argue that social interactions not only are largely unexplored in this field but also are an essential element of advanced cognitive ability, and therefore constitute metaphorically the “dark matter” of AI.

applications.justification: The paper discusses the potential outcomes of incorporating social learning theories and empirical findings into AI, suggesting applications in developing agents that can interact more naturally with humans and other agents.
applications.quote: Moreover, this section aims at demonstrating how social interactions are a key component of biological intelligence; we make the case that they might be of inspiration for the development of socially intelligent artificial agents that can cooperate efficiently with humans and with each other.
